title: Time over noise: Coordination with the unresolved inconsistencies of individual timing — code and data archive
description:
Code, simulation datasets and analysis results supporting the paper:

Sasai, K., Soga, Y. & Gunji, Y.-P. Time over noise: Coordination with the unresolved inconsistencies of individual timing. (2026, in revision.)

The paper asks whether the variability that coordination needs can come from the individuality of time itself, through the inconsistencies it produces, rather than from behavioral noise tuned from outside. It compares two decentralized update models on the distributed graph-coloring problem: the synchronous noise model (SNM; all agents act on a common clock, with behavioral noise ε) and the asynchronous random model (ARM; each agent acts on its own time with probability 1 − p and redraws its color at random only when gridlocked).

Contents. Source code (solver, runners, analyses, figure and table scripts; the GitHub release v2.2), the core simulation datasets (N = 20, k = 3; regenerated with the seeded solver and bit-reproducible on the platform and with the library versions in requirements-lock.txt), the parameter scans of Fig. 6, and the analysis results from which every figure and supplementary table is drawn. The .pkl files are gzip-compressed; uncompress them with gunzip. See README.md and docs/reproduction.md for the mapping from each figure and table to its scripts and data.

Version v1.0 contains the code and data of the first version of the manuscript.
